content:
maya: Heads up — seeing intermittent tail latency and token stalls on node gpu-12 in us-west-2, started ~09:04 UTC. TPS dips to 40% for a few mins then recovers. Likely thermal/power. infra-bot just fired an alert.

ross: :eyes: can you paste the nvidia-smi summary and any Xid/ECC entries from dmesg?

maya: Pasting quick snippets: 
```
$ nvidia-smi -q -d TEMPERATURE,POWER,PERFORMANCE
GPU 12:
  Temperature
    GPU Current Temp                     : 92 C
  Power Readings
    Power Draw                           : 310.50 W
    Power Limit                          : 320.00 W
  Performance State                      : P0
```
And dmesg shows repeated lines: `NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:af:00): 13, PID=2145` every ~2m. No ECC errors logged in the last hour.

jamal: 92C is high but under limit. The repeated Xid 13 is suspicious — we've seen that with flaky VRAM or occasional PCI resets. Any fan speed telemetry?

ev an: Node telemetry from prometheus: fan RPM for gpu-12 oscillates between 1100 and 3800 every 30-90s. Temp spikes coincide with RPM drops.

maya: Also noticed one of the chassis PDUs reported short power sag at 09:03:16: `pdu-7: power_event TYPE=INRUSH` — correlates with first Xid.

ross: So two correlated signals: fan speed oscillation (sensor or controller issue) + brief PDU event. Could be a board-level fan controller reset causing a short thermal excursion and the driver hitting Xid.

infra-bot: Alert created: GPU_THERMAL_ANOMALY #4567 (node: gpu-12, region: us-west-2)

maya: Quick mitigation — can we drain the node and failover inference traffic? We have Dedicated pools in us-west-2 and can route to standby.

jamal: I'm +1 on drain. If we don't drain, repeated Xids will degrade KV cache and cause inference stalls. Recommend `kubectl cordon` + `drain --delete-local-data` for the node before replacement.

ross: Also create temporary routing rule to shift 30% of traffic to us-west-1 and 20% to dedicated-burst-cap. Keep 50% local to avoid wholesale capacity churn.

maya: Doing drain now. Command I ran: `kubectl drain gpu-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force` — pods are rescheduling.

evan: Can infra team also pull GPU telemetry logs and nvml dump before power cycling? If it's an intermittent controller reset, a graceful power cycle might clear it but we need logs first.

maya: nvml logs saved to /var/log/gpu/gpu-12-nvml-1769501234.log and uploaded to s3://redwood-gpu-telemetry/us-west-2/gpu-12/1769501234.log

jamal: If we see persistent Xid 13 after powercycle, schedule replacement. Also check SMBus temp sensor readouts — sometimes the sensor/drivers misreport leading to fan controller thrash.

ross: Ops runbook reminder: Xid 13 often maps to `GPU hardware exception / ECC not correctable` or driver timeouts depending on driver version. We should note driver version and kernel oopses in the incident.

maya: Driver: 525.85.12, kernel: 6.1.17. No ECC corrected/uncorrected counters incremented though.

infra-bot: Runbook step triggered: create incident doc and tag oncall. Incident created: INF-2026-0421.

evan: After drain, I'll power-cycle the chassis and keep it out of rotation for 24h, then run extended memtest and stress test (memtestG80 + heavy attention load).

maya: Can someone confirm cost/latency impact from traffic shift? We should notify product if 30% routes to higher-cost region.

ross: Quick estimate: shifting 30% to us-west-1 adds ~12% egress + inter-region overhead for those requests; cost team notified via pager. Latency P50 increases ~8ms for affected routes.

jamal: If replacement needed, check spare pool inventory: we have 4 pluggable Ampere cards in on-site stock; request RMA for the board while we swap.

maya: Post-powercycle note (09:18 UTC): fans stabilized, temp dropped to 67C, Xid messages stopped for 10m. Putting node into limited traffic mode for diagnostics.

ross: Good. Keep it in limited traffic and observe 1h. If Xid returns, mark for replacement. If stable, reintroduce to pool with canary traffic.

evan: Added a Grafana panel to show synchronized fan RPM + PDU events to catch similar correlated failures. Saved dashboard URL: https://grafana.redwood.com/d/GPUs/gpu-thermal-correlation

maya: Thanks everyone. I'll update the incident doc with logs and next steps. Moral: we should add a synthetic probe for fan RPM variance > 50% in <2m and auto-drain to avoid decode/regression during inference peaks.

ross: Agreed. Filing an Optimize task to evaluate auto-drain thresholds vs cost impact. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: Incident INF-2026-0421 status updated: mitigation in progress.

maya: If anyone wants the nvml dump or canary config, ping me.

jamal: pinged. grabbing nvml dump now.

ross: Closing loop later after 1h stable run. Thanks all.
